r.summary: Source reading only; nothing was built, edited or committed. In WordPress 7.2-RC2 PostLockedModal reads only the core/editor store, and that state can be written with three public (non-unlock) actions: setEditedPost, updateEditorSettings and updatePostLock. Filling the store is not enough for the behaviour in data-model.md Locks: the modal cannot be dismissed, both its buttons are fixed hrefs to wp-admin (post.php and edit.php), it releases the lock only on page unload, and it takes a first lock only through a heartbeat tick (60 s default interval). If the first encounter with another user's lock arrives by heartbeat, the modal shows the "taken over" wording with no "Take over" button, so the plugin needs its own server call at enter-edit under options A, B and C. WordPress 7.2-RC2 has no REST lock route and ships no collaboration PHP or sync script, so the classic _edit_lock is the only mechanism. WordPress for Writers is on this machine; it uses EditorProvider (which this spec excludes) and takes the lock in PHP at page load, so it is not a precedent for this plugin's case.

options.name: B. Same allowlist change, but the plugin handles takeover itself
options.evidence:
The modal's links cannot be changed from JavaScript through any public surface: no props, hard-coded hrefs (editor.js:98307-98319), filter wrapper compiled out (98413).

The only public server hooks on the takeover path: wp-admin/post.php:158-163 calls wp_redirect( get_edit_post_link( $post_id, 'url' ) ). "Exit editor" is a plain link to edit.php?post_type=... with no hook that could send it back to the board.

No filter or argument lets a non-editor screen take the lock on page load; the screen-independent paths are the heartbeat handler (misc.php:1257, ignores $screen_id) and calling wp_set_post_lock from plugin PHP.

options.name: C. Drop PostLockedModal; specify a plugin lock dialog on the classic lock functions
options.evidence:
Everything the stock dialog does is reachable through public surfaces without the core/editor store:
- Check and take: wp_check_post_lock / wp_set_post_lock (wp-admin/includes/post.php:1744, 1789), both already on api-allowlist.md line 49. In REST context post.php must be required first, as core does at wp-includes/rest-api/endpoints/class-wp-rest-autosaves-controller.php:228-230.

Using it needs `@wordpress/hooks` addAction/removeAction, which is not on the allowlist; a plugin REST route polled by the plugin avoids that.
- Release: wp_ajax_wp_remove_post_lock (wp-admin/includes/ajax-actions.php:2902-2937) sets the lock time to now - 150 + 5 if the stored value equals active_post_lock and the user matches; needs nonce update-post_{id}. A plugin route can do the same with update_post_meta.
- Takeover is just wp_set_post_lock by the new user (post.php:160); the previous holder then gets lock_error on the next refresh (misc.php:1272-1286).

No core REST lock route exists: grep of wp-includes/rest-api for _edit_lock, post_lock, wp_check_post_lock, wp_set_post_lock matches only the autosaves controller (:228-246), which reads the lock to choose between updating a draft and creating an autosave revision.

options.costsAndRisks: Two administrators on the same page: neither is warned. Administrator 1 in wp-admin's editor holds the lock; administrator 2 on the board sees no dialog, edits and saves; the REST save succeeds. Whoever saves last overwrites the other's content in full; the earlier version survives only as a revision. In the other direction, because the board takes no lock, wp-admin's editor shows administrator 1 no "already being edited" dialog while administrator 2 is editing on the board. Two people on two boards editing the same page have the same exposure. Templates, template parts and global styles already have no lock in the spec, so this extends an existing gap to pages and patterns. Smallest spec change and it unblocks the Milestone 0 gate for OQ-2 immediately.

r.recommendation: Choose between C and D; A and B do not deliver what data-model.md asks for. With the stock modal, a locked page always ends with the user leaving the board (non-dismissible dialog, two wp-admin links), and the plugin needs its own server route anyway for the first lock, the correct first-encounter wording and the release on leaving edit. If two people working on the same site is a real case for this version, take C: it is the only option that keeps "the artboard stays read-only unless the user takes over", at the price of one new screen and about ten wording and behaviour decisions from the owner. If it is not, take D: it is the smallest change and unblocks the gate, with the stated consequence that concurrent edits to a page silently overwrite each other and wp-admin's editor gets no warning. A is only worth choosing if being sent to wp-admin's editor on a locked page is acceptable; B adds a referer-based redirect and a full board reload for little gain over A.
unverified: Nothing was run for this question; every statement is from reading source. The redirect-filter approach in B, the plugin routes in C and the overwrite behaviour in D were not executed.

What autosave() does when no post is set in core/editor: savePost returns early if isEditedPostSaveable is false (editor.js:8013), but I did not trace isEditedPostEmpty with a null post type and id, so whether it returns early or throws is not established. With setEditedPost called it reaches saveEntityRecord with isAutosave (8040-8050).

Side effects of calling setEditedPost / updateEditorSettings on the shared core/editor store for EntitiesSavedStates, UnsavedChangesWarning, EditorSnackbars or blocks that read that store were not checked.

That the heartbeat script is loaded on the board app page: wp_auth_check_load is hooked on admin_enqueue_scripts (wp-includes/default-filters.php:525) and wp-auth-check depends on heartbeat (script-loader.php:858), but the board page prints without wp-admin chrome (architecture.md line 11) and I did not confirm it keeps that hook.
Whether a `@wordpress/hooks` import or the `wp.heartbeat` global would be acceptable under C1; neither is on the allowlist.
WordPress for Writers takeover behaviour was inferred from the absence of any get-post-lock or redirect handling in its source, not observed.
The update-core.php comment says sync.js was restored in 7.1, yet the file is absent from this 7.2-RC2 install; I report the absence as measured and did not investigate why.
The spec was checked against 7.2-beta5 and Gutenberg e77b5057a91; all line numbers here are from the 7.2-RC2 files and may differ in the final release.

r.summary: Source reading of WordPress 7.2-RC2 block-editor.js and components.js shows two independent defects under any scale other than 1. (1) CoverContainer sizes itself from selectedElement.offsetWidth/offsetHeight (block-editor.js:98900-98905), which ignore every transform, so all six BlockPopoverCover users are mis-sized whenever tools and canvas are not at the same scale. (2) floating-ui divides the anchor rect by the offset parent's scale, multiplies by the iframe's scale, then adds the iframe's already-scaled viewport offset undivided (components.js:8875-8910, 9136-9166), so with a transform on an ancestor of BlockTools every popover inside it is displaced by iframeViewportOffset x (z - 1); with the spike's iframe top of 121 px this predicts -60.5 px at 50% and -30.25 px at 75%, and the spike measured -60.3 and -30.4. Core has no path that shows a scaled canvas with fully working tools: its zoom-out puts `scale` on the iframe's <html> (the spike's failing "inner" arrangement) and switches the tools off rather than correcting them (block-editor.js:106593, 106614, 99198, 100754, 106054-106059). The private path named in OQ-1 (ExperimentalBlockCanvas iframeProps) therefore does not fix the cover popovers. Only 100% was measured passing, so the workable resolutions are A (edit at 100% only) or a 100%-pop-out form of B, which is A's requirement plus a second transform and overlap.

4. GridVisualizer 135073-135100 (used 136265, 136820): grid cell outlines and drop targets; slot "__unstable-block-tools-after" (rendered inside BlockTools, 106621-106627). Tracks come from computed style in layout px (134958-134999). (i) wrong position; (ii)/(iii) cells 1/z too large, do not line up with the real grid. From source.

Same mis-size; onResizeStop also mixes offsetLeft/Top/Width/Height (135524-135529) with pointer deltas, and no `scale` prop is passed to ResizableBox (135477-135500) although re-resizable supports one (components.js:71792, 71852), so the handle and the result diverge at any scale != 1. 8. BlockToolbarPopover 106201-106249: anchor from getElementBounds = getBoundingClientRect (67296-67325, 98808-98817). Not rendered when hasFixedToolbar (106378), which D7 requires, so not applicable. Its only offset* read is popoverNode.offsetHeight for the flip decision (101736).

Inside the iframe, unaffected in all three: useMovingAnimation offsetTop/offsetLeft (67115-67120, layout-space animation), ZoomOutSeparator 100474-100550 (in-canvas element, zoom-out mode only), block overlay state 15310-15322 (no geometry), reflow-only reads 133959 and 68085. List view drop indicator offsetWidth 108678 is outside the canvas.

options.name: B. Live artboard drawn in an unscaled layer over its frame while the board stays at the user's zoom
options.whatTheSpecWouldHaveToSay:
Two readings, and the spec would have to choose.
B1 (layer unscaled, artboard scaled to fit its frame): this is the spike's "counter" (ii) or "inner" (iii) arrangement. No spec wording makes it pass.
B2 (layer unscaled, artboard shown at 100% regardless of board zoom, anchored to its frame's top-left): constraints.md C22 "They change one CSS transform." -> "They change the canvas transform and the Live layer's transform."; architecture.md `viewport` row "Writes one CSS transform on the canvas surface per animation frame" and Data streams Viewport row "One CSS transform" likewise; architecture.md Tiers Live row gains "drawn at 100% in a layer above the canvas surface"; screens/README.md A3 "The tier content at the device width, scaled by the zoom" needs "except Live"; C18 and D30 can keep 50% as the board zoom needed to enter edit, or drop the threshold; a new decision row must say what the Live artboard covers and how it is reached when it extends past the canvas. AC-PERF-01 "the canvas transform changes each frame" -> also the Live layer's; AC-CANVAS-03 must define zoom with the pointer over the Live artboard.
options.evidence:
B1: measured FAIL. counter and inner at 50%/75%: add-block button 24 px at x 1636-1660 against an anchor ending at 940 / 1300 (/Users/andreidraganescu/Sites/wordpress-for-designers/spikes/evidence/a-counter.json, a-inner.json); cause block-editor.js:98900-98905.
B2: from source only. With cumulative scale 1 on both the tools and the iframe, offsetWidth equals visual width and floating-ui's scale terms are 1 (components.js:8824-8846, 8893-8904). The spike's 100% runs are the nearest measurement but they used scale(1), not scale(z) with an inner scale(1/z); that exact nesting is unmeasured.
C9 check: the layer is in the same document and can sit under the same RegistryProvider, so "one document... one core-data registry... No iframe page per editor" holds (BlockCanvas's iframe is the stock in-document canvas either way).
C22 check: the layer must follow its frame during pan and zoom. Either a second transform is written each frame, or the layer is nested in the surface with a counter-scale that changes with every zoom frame. Both are more than "one CSS transform" as C22 is worded. No React render is needed, so AC-PERF-01's render-count half can still hold.
options.costsAndRisks: B2 gesture behaviour: the Live artboard does not change size on Cmd/Ctrl+wheel while everything around it does; at 50% a Desktop artboard is drawn 1440 px wide over a 720 px frame and covers whatever is to the right and below (1/z overlap), blocking select and move on those artboards; zoom "around the pointer" (AC-CANVAS-03) has no natural meaning while the pointer is over an element that does not scale; pan moves the layer by translate. options.whatTheSpecWouldHaveToSay: api-allowlist.md would gain a row such as "`@wordpress/block-editor` | WP script | `privateApis`: `ExperimentalBlockCanvas` (prop `iframeProps.scale`) | Private, only in `src/adapter/private.js`", the "Not allowed" list line 44 already permits that file, and C2's open-questions precondition is met by OQ-1. options.evidence:
ExperimentalBlockCanvas 107083-107169 passes `iframeProps` to Iframe and, when the store zoom level is not 100, adds scale and frameSize "40px" (107106-107109). Iframe 74478-74651 hands `scale` to useScaleCanvas 74047 onward, which only sets custom properties and the `is-zoomed-out` class on the iframe's documentElement (74131-74135, 74166, 74185-74213). The CSS then applies `scale: var(--wp-block-editor-iframe-zoom-out-scale)` to `.block-editor-iframe__html.is-zoomed-out` (node_modules/@wordpress/block-editor/build-style/content.css:861-868, package 20.1.0, not the RC2 file). That is a transform on <html> inside the iframe: the spike's "inner" arrangement, measured failing. Nothing in CoverContainer reads the scale; the only JS consumer of the scale property is ZoomOutSeparator (100540).
Core's own answer is to switch tools off in zoom-out, not correct them: isZoomOut = zoomLevel < 100 or "auto-scaled" (13301-13303); InsertionPoint not rendered (106593); "block-toolbar" popover slot not rendered (106614); in-between inserter disabled (99198); appender hidden (100754); toolbar slots, group, lock and visibility buttons hidden (106054-106059); block editing modes re-derived for sections (8726-8727); drop feedback moved into the canvas as ZoomOutSeparator sized with calc(frame-size / scale) (100474-100550) and outlines divided by the scale in CSS (content.css:220-222, 309-311, 480). setZoomLevel/resetZoomLevel are private actions (15435, 15450, 15459) and useZoomOut is private (97560, 138128). So the private store path gives a scaled canvas with reduced tools, and the iframeProps path gives a scaled canvas with the same mis-sized covers. CoverContainer and BlockPopoverCover are not exported, publicly or privately (private list 138090-138140 has PrivateBlockPopover and ResizableBoxPopover only).
options.costsAndRisks: Spends the C2 exception and adds an API that can change without notice, for no gain on the measured failure. Setting the store zoom level would also change editing behaviour inside the artboard (section-only selection), against C6.
options.specItemsAffected: C1, C2 or C3, api-allowlist.md rows and "Not allowed" list. Would leave blocked: Milestone 0 gate, C18, D30, AC-EDIT-04, AC-TIER-07.

r.recommendation: Choose A (edit at exactly 100%). It is the only resolution with a measured pass, it needs no allowlist change, and the source shows why it is exact: both defects are functions of scale != 1 and nothing in core corrects them. Do not choose C: the path OQ-1 names (ExperimentalBlockCanvas iframeProps) scales <html> inside the iframe, which is the spike's failing "inner" arrangement, and core's zoom-out hides the affected tools instead of fixing them. If keeping neighbouring artboards visible while editing matters more than simplicity, B2 (Live artboard popped out at 100% over a board that stays at the user's zoom) is the fallback, but it needs C22 reworded to allow a second transform, a decision about overlap and zoom-over-Live behaviour, and one more spike of the scale(z) outer / scale(1/z) inner nesting before the gate can pass. Whichever is chosen, the Milestone 0 (a) text and api-allowlist line 58 must be rewritten so the gate tests the arrangement actually specified. Before committing to A, the product owner should look at a 1440 px Desktop artboard at 100% between the two panels, since that is the main cost.

r.summary: On WordPress 7.2-RC2 the stock PostLockedModal can be made to run the whole lock lifecycle with three non-allowlisted core/editor actions (setEditedPost, updateEditorSettings, updatePostLock) plus the heartbeat script, but only with plugin PHP supplying postLock and postLockUtils per post. Even then it does not give the behaviour in data-model.md Locks: the modal covers the whole 1440x900 viewport, cannot be dismissed (Esc and click-through both measured blocked), and its only exits leave the board (Take over lands on /wp-admin/post.php?post=11&action=edit, Exit editor on /wp-admin/edit.php?post_type=page). Leaving edit does not release the lock: unmounting the modal or clearing the editor post left _edit_lock unchanged; the stock release fires only on beforeunload. Switching the current post with setEditedPost alone leaks lock state from one post to the next, never releases the first post's lock, and makes the release for the second post fail with 403. A prototype without the modal (plugin REST route around wp_check_post_lock / wp_set_post_lock, api-fetch, a components Modal) took, refreshed, detected, took over and released the lock without leaving the board and interoperated with the core editor in both directions; it needs the spec to define the dialog text and controls. Raw data is in /Users/andreidraganescu/Sites/wordpress-for-designers/spikes/diag-oq2/results.json with screenshots alongside.

options.name: A. Stock PostLockedModal fed through three core/editor store actions, stock links accepted
options.whatTheSpecWouldHaveToSay: api-allowlist.md, @wordpress/editor row: add `store` with actions `setEditedPost`, `updateEditorSettings`, `updatePostLock` (selectors optional: `isPostLocked`, `getActivePostLock`). Add the `heartbeat` script handle as a required enqueue (architecture.md Editor bootstrap) and state the interval (default measured 60 s; core's editor sets 10 s with wp.heartbeat.interval( 10 ) in edit-form-blocks.php:208, which is a global, not an import). PHP list: add `wp_create_nonce`, `get_userdata`, `get_avatar_url`, `register_rest_route` (or say nonces are minted at page load for every page/pattern on the board). data-model.md Locks must be rewritten to say: (1) the lock is taken by the first heartbeat after entering edit, not at once; (2) the plugin must itself call admin-ajax `wp-remove-post-lock` when the artboard leaves edit, and must reset `updatePostLock` and `postLockUtils` before each `setEditedPost`; (3) when another user holds the lock the dialog blocks the whole board and the user can only go to the post editor (Take over) or the Pages list (Exit editor); 'the artboard stays read-only unless the user takes over' has to be deleted. AC-EDIT-06 reworded to match. Also state that a takeover triggers a core autosave of the page.
options.evidence:
Source: editor.js:98196-98420 (modal reads only core/editor; heartbeat.send/tick hooks; release only on beforeunload at 98294; links hard-coded at 98309-98319; withFilters is dead code at 98420). PHP: edit-form-blocks.php:229-263 and 286-290 produce postLock/postLockUtils (nonces 'lock-post_ID', 'update-post_ID'); misc.php:1257-1299 heartbeat handler sets the lock when free; ajax-actions.php:2902-2937 release.
Measured (results.json):
- E1a: free page, setEditedPost only: lock taken after 60 s (first natural heartbeat), meta 1795080912:1, activePostLock stored, no errors. So no initial PHP/REST lock call is strictly needed, but there is up to a 60 s gap.
- E1a3: without postLockUtils, leaving the page throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading unlockNonce)' and the lock is not released. E1a2: with postLockUtils, navigating away moved the lock time back to 146 s old (core keeps it valid for the other user about 5 more seconds).
- E1b_i: locked by 'second', setEditedPost only: on heartbeat the modal throws (reading 'nonce') and the whole React root unmounts (#wfd-b count 0). So updateEditorSettings({postLockUtils}) is mandatory.
- E1b_ii: setEditedPost + postLockUtils, no updatePostLock: modal appears only after a heartbeat and with the wrong wording: 'Someone else has taken over this post', no Take over button; it also POSTed /wp/v2/pages/11/autosaves although nothing was dirty.
- E1b_iii: all three actions with PHP-provided postLock {isLocked:true,user}: 'This post is already being edited', links Take over -> post.php?get-post-lock=1&lockKey=true&post=11&action=edit&_wpnonce=..., Exit editor -> edit.php?post_type=page. Overlay rect 0,0,1440x900; click on a button behind it did not reach it; modal still shown after Escape; no close button. Admin's heartbeat while locked did not overwrite second's lock.
- E1c: unmounting the modal: meta unchanged; later heartbeat sends no lock data (so the lock silently expires after 150 s); setEditedPost(null,null): meta unchanged, activePostLock stays in the store.
- E1d: takeover by 'second' in the real editor detected on admin's next heartbeat: 'Someone else has taken over this post', only 'Exit editor'; the modal's autosave() POSTed /wp/v2/pages/11/autosaves and created autosave revision '11-autosave-v1' with the unsaved title; the entity stayed dirty.
- E3: Take over lands on /wp-admin/post.php?post=11&action=edit (meta :1); Exit editor lands on /wp-admin/edit.php?post_type=page.
- E2 switch: setEditedPost to a second page alone: first page's lock not released (age 4 s on leave), stale activePostLock sent, release for the second page answered 403 (nonce is per post), and a locked state from page A showed the modal on free page B with B's Take over link.
- E2 side effects with a dirty page for 75 s: 0 autosave POSTs, no notices, no console errors, EntitiesSavedStates text unchanged; only two extra GETs (types/page, pages/11/autosaves).
options.costsAndRisks: Does not meet data-model.md Locks as written: no read-only state on the board is reachable, both exits leave the app (unsaved template/part artboards that exist only in the session would be lost; UnsavedChangesWarning would fire). Plugin must still write lock plumbing (per-post nonces, reset on switch, explicit release call), so the 'stock' part is only the dialog. Global side effect read from source, not measured: core blocks read core/editor's current post on the shared registry (block-library.js calendar/edit, query-title/use-archive-label and use-post-type-label, term-count, utils/is-within-overlay), so setting it changes what those blocks compute in every artboard. The modal returns null when real-time collaboration is enabled for the post (editor.js:98299, 7249-7266); not exercised here. PostLockedModal uses unlock() internally, so it can change without notice. Dialog text says 'post' for pages and patterns.
options.specItemsAffected: C1 (allowlist grows by a store), C6/C7 unaffected, D28 (holds, with a delay up to one heartbeat), data-model.md Locks (sentence 'stays read-only unless the user takes over' cannot hold), AC-EDIT-06 (must be reworded), api-allowlist.md Known risks first bullet, architecture.md Editor bootstrap (heartbeat).

Add `add_filter`, `wp_get_referer` to the PHP list. State that after the reload the artboard that was being entered is re-entered (needs a URL parameter the spec must name) and that Exit editor still goes to the Pages list.

Public filters on that path: 'get_edit_post_link' (link-template.php:1506) and 'wp_redirect' (pluggable.php:1506). options.name: B. No PostLockedModal: plugin REST route around wp_check_post_lock / wp_set_post_lock, api-fetch, a design-system dialog
options.whatTheSpecWouldHaveToSay: api-allowlist.md: remove `PostLockedModal` from the @wordpress/editor row and delete the first Known-risks bullet's PostLockedModal half; PHP list add `register_rest_route`, `get_userdata`, `get_avatar_url`, `delete_post_meta`/`update_post_meta` (for release), and the note that `wp_check_post_lock`/`wp_set_post_lock` need `require_once ABSPATH . 'wp-admin/includes/post.php'` in REST requests. architecture.md: name the route (for example `wfd/v1/lock/{id}`: POST take or refresh, POST with takeover, DELETE release; permission `edit_theme_options` and `edit_post`) and the refresh interval (must be under the 150 s lock window; core uses 10 s in its editor, 60 s elsewhere). data-model.md Locks: replace 'the stock lock dialog (PostLockedModal) is shown' with a plugin dialog. A new screens/ entry with a component map (for example `AlertDialog` from @wordpress/ui) must define, verbatim: (1) title when the entity is locked on entering edit; (2) body naming the user, and whether the avatar is shown; (3) button that takes over; (4) button that keeps the artboard read-only, and whether Esc/close does the same; (5) title and body when another user takes over while this user is editing, and its buttons; (6) what happens to this user's unsaved edits at that moment (core autosaves; the board has no autosave); (7) the read-only indicator on the artboard label or document bar and the control to take over later; (8) the message when a lock request fails; (9) whether a read-only artboard becomes editable by itself when the lock frees. Core's own wording could be adopted as the spec text if wanted: 'This post is already being edited', 'Someone else has taken over this post', '%s is currently working on this post (preview), which means you cannot make changes, unless you take over.', 'If you take over, the other user will lose editing control to the post, but their changes will be saved.', 'Take over', 'Exit editor' (these say 'post' and go through the plugin text domain under C23). AC-EDIT-06: replace 'the stock lock dialog appears' with the new dialog's name.
options.evidence:
Prototype: spike 'd' in /Users/andreidraganescu/Sites/wordpress-for-designers/spikes/wfd-diag2/src/index.js (client imports all allowlisted: api-fetch, element, components Modal/Button) and the route in wfd-diag2.php. Measured:

r.recommendation: Choose option B. It is the only one measured to deliver what data-model.md Locks and AC-EDIT-06 actually ask for (lock on entering edit, release on leaving, read-only artboard with an in-place takeover, takeover detection) and it keeps the allowlist free of the core/editor store. The price is a spec change the product owner has to write: one small dialog screen with its strings and buttons, a read-only indicator, the route name and the refresh interval; core's own wording can be copied to keep it familiar. Option A is the smaller allowlist edit but it does not produce the specified behaviour: the stock dialog blocks the whole board and both of its buttons leave the app, and the plugin still has to write release, reset-on-switch and nonce plumbing around it. If the stock dialog is a hard requirement, A2 is the least bad form, accepting a full board reload on takeover. Separate finding for the spec owner: the allowlisted `EditorSnackbars` logs 'deprecated since version 7.0 and will be removed in version 7.2. Please use wp.notices.SnackbarNotices' on 7.2-RC2.

Ten checks (the six originals plus in-between inserter, grid visualizer, grid item resizer, cover-block resize box) all pass at 100% with the public BlockCanvas. The only arrangement that passed all ten at 50% and 75% was the public "counter" arrangement plus plugin CSS that rescales core's cover container; it uses no private JS API but targets core class names and inline styles, and the cover-block resize drag then moves at z times the pointer (30 px for a 60 px drag at 50%, 45 px at 75%; 60 px at 100%). A plugin can obtain unlock on RC2 by calling the opt-in from the wp-private-apis script handle with a core module name and the exact consent string; there is no duplicate-registration or caller check, so constraint C2's adapter file is technically usable but would not help OQ-1.

options.name: Finding: can a plugin obtain unlock on 7.2-RC2 (usability of src/adapter/private.js, C2)
options.whatTheSpecWouldHaveToSay: If any private API is ever allowed: api-allowlist.md must name '@wordpress/private-apis' (WP script handle wp-private-apis, never bundled) and state that src/adapter/private.js calls __dangerousOptInToUnstableAPIsOnlyForCoreModules with the exact consent string and a borrowed core module name (for example '@wordpress/block-editor'), wrapped in try/catch with a defined fallback, and that this impersonates a core module against the API's stated terms.
options.evidence: Measured (probes.optIn): from a plugin script depending on wp-private-apis, calling the opt-in with the RC2 consent string and module name '@wordpress/block-editor', '@wordpress/edit-site' or '@wordpress/theme' returned a working unlock (unlock(privateApis) of block-editor exposed 92 keys including ExperimentalBlockCanvas; unlock on the store's select/dispatch gave getZoomLevel, isZoomOut, setZoomLevel). Names not on the list ('wordpress-for-designers', '@wordpress/not-a-core-module') threw 'You tried to opt-in to unstable APIs as module ...'. A wrong consent string threw. Source (wp-includes/js/dist/private-apis.js in RC2): the only checks are CORE_MODULES_USING_PRIVATE_APIS.includes(moduleName) and consent === requiredConsent; there is no already-registered check and no caller check. lockedData is a module-scoped WeakMap keyed through a module-scoped Symbol, so only the wp.privateApis instance core scripts use can unlock core objects; a copy bundled from npm cannot (from source, not run). node_modules/@wordpress/private-apis 3.2.0 carries the same consent string.
options.costsAndRisks: Fragile in three independent ways: the consent string is a literal that must match exactly (it states the API 'will break in the next version'); the core-module list can change; every unlocked member (ExperimentalBlockCanvas, iframeProps.scale, setZoomLevel) can be renamed or removed without notice. A mismatch throws at module load, which would blank the whole plugin unless caught. Whether WordPress.org plugin review accepts this is unverified.
options.specItemsAffected: C2, api-allowlist.md 'Not allowed'. Does not unblock OQ-1 by itself (options 1 and 2 fail).

r.recommendation: Do not open the private adapter for OQ-1: both private paths were measured and neither fixes the cover controls (option 1 fails the same four checks; option 2 disables editing). The real choice is between option 4 and option 3. Option 4 (edit at 100% only) is the only one that passed everything, including resize-by-drag, with no dependence on core internals; it costs a change to C18/D30 and the AddArtboard flow. Option 3 keeps editing at 50-100% with no new imports and passed all ten placement checks, but it rests on CSS aimed at core's private DOM and leaves resize handles dragging at z times pointer speed, so it needs an explicit exception in C5/C6 and a regression test. If editing below 100% is a firm product requirement, take option 3 with those two additions; otherwise take option 4.
unverified: Block drop-zone indicator (BlockDropZonePopover, a BlockPopoverCover user at block-editor.js:98928-98950) was not triggered or measured in any mode.
Padding/margin spacing visualizer (cover user near block-editor.js:132769) was not measured; it needs an inspector control hover.
Manual-grid visualizer cells/appenders and image block resize handles were not measured; only the auto grid visualizer, grid item resizer box and the cover block's ResizableBoxPopover were.
That a copy of @wordpress/private-apis bundled from npm cannot unlock core objects is read from source (module-scoped Symbol and WeakMap), not run.
History of the consent string across WordPress versions and whether it will change after 7.2 was not checked; only the RC2 string and the npm 3.2.0 string were read (identical).
Whether WordPress.org plugin review permits calling the opt-in with a core module name was not checked.
Option 4's variant where only the Live artboard is unscaled inside a board zoomed to another level was not built; only whole-view 100% was measured.
The CSS fix of option 3 was measured on the counter and expscale arrangements only, not on the inner arrangement, and only in Chromium at 1440x900.
Why clicks time out in zoom-out mode (option 2) was not traced to a specific source line; only the behaviour was measured.

A user who is blocked or has just lost the lock can still save that page through Review, because core REST saves ignore _edit_lock (review-1.mjs R1). The spec must state it (leave it saveable, uncheck it, or block it); otherwise option B gives a dialog but not protection.

Risk for option B, measured: the route's check-then-set is not atomic. With two users posting at the same moment, both were told 'held' in 5 of 8 rounds (review-1.mjs R6); the meta ends up with one of them and the other only finds out at its next refresh. Core has the same class of race, but the spec's refresh interval sets how long two people can both believe they hold the lock.

Risk for option B, measured: a blocked user never re-checks. After the holder released the lock the blocked session still showed 'blocked' 7 s later (R5), because the prototype refreshes only while holding. The owner has to decide whether a blocked artboard retries on the next attempt to enter edit only (simplest) or polls.
